claims.text: MLIPs trained on ab initio liquid configurations will represent the configurational space of high-temperature solid and liquid high-entropy alloys better than traditional EAM reference potentials.
Neural-network potentials and Gaussian approximation potentials can be trained on ab initio liquid configurations and used as references in thermodynamic integration.
The proposed intervention applies to near-equiatomic alloys containing five or more elements.
The proposed temperature range is approximately 1500–3000 K near the alloy melting point.
Liquid-like disorder near melting substantially expands the atomic configuration space.
MLIP descriptors of local atomic environments map the diverse configurations of an ab initio liquid better than EAM potentials.
EAM potentials primarily capture average behavior and inadequately represent the diverse configurations of an ab initio liquid.
Training on a broad sample of ab initio configurations allows MLIPs to learn a nonlinear, high-fidelity representation of interatomic interactions.
A higher-fidelity representation of interatomic interactions will produce smoother thermodynamic-integration paths.
More accurate representation of the target interactions will increase phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target states.
MLIP references will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 25–50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
MLIP-based integration will yield more accurate free energies and reduce systematic errors in high-temperature ab initio free-energy estimates.
Standard TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references exhibit notable phase-space sampling mismatch relative to the ab initio liquid at high temperatures.
The intervention may cease to be effective for elemental or binary systems with limited configurational diversity or at temperatures far from melting.
Analogous successes of MLIP-based integration have been observed in simpler elemental or binary systems.
